data.analysis: Keep N=3: scalar loop scheduling and SIMD mapping are distinct opportunities, but the original T1/T2 objectives overlap substantially because both broadly ask for SIMD mapping and packing, differing mainly in width. Make their mapping mechanisms explicit so results contrast: AVX2 arithmetic classification versus AVX-512VBMI table permutation. Also make short-input and vector-boundary padding tests explicit; “varied lengths” alone may miss tail errors. The supplied one-core workload does not justify a separate threading tree. Treat AVX-512 support as conditional on the frozen build: GCC’s znver4 feature list is not proof of the compile flags or a performance win.

revisions.objective: In its own research branch, modify only src/candidate.cpp to evaluate an AVX2 decoder whose primary mapping method is vector range classification and arithmetic offsets, followed by vector bit packing—not a wide table-permute lookup. Use safe block loads/stores and a correct tail/padding path; verify ISA support under the frozen build without changing flags. Preserve exact output semantics and stay within the threads budget. Validate empty and short strings plus lengths around vector-block boundaries, all padding cases, random valid inputs, and the official Lena input before repeated native timing. Do not specialize to its length; record failures and results.
revisions.subject: AVX2 arithmetic-classification decoder

revisions.objective: In its own research branch, modify only src/candidate.cpp to evaluate a distinct AVX-512VBMI table-permutation approach for mapping Base64 input bytes to six-bit values, then pack decoded bytes. Do not merely widen T1’s loop: contrast its mapping strategy explicitly. Verify the required instructions are enabled by the frozen build and supported by the target; do not change compiler flags or assume 512-bit execution is faster. Use safe loads/stores and correct tails/padding, preserve exact output semantics, and respect the threads budget. Validate empty and short strings, lengths around vector-block boundaries, every padding case, random valid inputs, and the official Lena input before repeated native timing; record unsupported-ISA and performance failures.
revisions.subject: AVX-512VBMI permutation decoder

revisions.objective: In its own research branch, modify only src/candidate.cpp to test scalar scheduling improvements to the existing table-driven eight-character/six-byte decode loop: unroll multiple independent groups so table lookups can overlap and loop overhead is amortized. Keep this a scalar-focused contrast to the SIMD trees; do not add explicit SIMD or parallel execution. Preserve exact output semantics, safe tails/padding, and the threads budget. Validate empty and short strings, lengths around the unrolled-group boundary, every padding case, random valid inputs, and the official Lena input before repeated native timing. Do not specialize to the benchmark length; record unsuccessful unroll/group-size choices and results.
revisions.subject: Scalar table-loop unrolling
